exact_missing_items: A canonical internal route payload schema must be defined in one doc (Contracts_V0.md or FinalGUISpec.md)
Minimum required fields for all route payloads: surface_id, object_kind, object_id (or object_ref), project_id?
Optional fields depending on surface: run_id, attempt_id, node_id, concern_id, attention_item_id, focus_sub_tab, lane_id, worktree_id
route payload is used by: deep links, palette actions, cmd.*.open_in_* commands, attention item primary_route_payload, and resume_url serialization

Concern user actions must include: open/focus, open evidence, open history, open ledger, acknowledge (where allowed), dismiss (where allowed), open resolution thread, approve/reject at HITL boundaries
Define the canonical `target_kind` enum in `Contracts_V0.md`.

The canonical vocabulary is: `primary_view` (full primary-content destinations: Dashboard, Projects, Wizard, Interview, Settings, Usage, Orchestrator); `side_panel` (activity-bar panel destinations: chat, files, source_control, github_actions, docker_manager, artifacts, run_debug); `bottom_panel` (bottom shell destinations: terminal, problems, output, ports, browser, debug); `embedded_surface` (embedded sub-surfaces: document_pane, agent_activity); `page_tab` (tab within a routed page: Orchestrator tabs)
Keep destination-local refinements outside the enum and outside the base route contract.
Use `page_tab` when the routed destination must land inside a known page and force a specific tab.
What is not `target_kind`: docked vs floating; panel width; widget slot; subview id; repo/worktree selection; browser tab id; workspace tab id
Define the closed `inspector_target` enum in `Contracts_V0.md`.
The canonical vocabulary is: `summary`; `evidence`; `artifacts`; `history`; `reviews`; `usage`; `lineage`; `details`
`inspector_target` is not object identity. `inspector_target` is not a per-surface arbitrary bag. `inspector_target` does not replace `tab_id`.
`wizard_step`, `message_id`, `line`, `range`, and compare-target state are not `inspector_target` values.
Use `inspector_target` only after primary selector identity is already established.
Use `inspector_target = lineage` for scheduler/remediation/safe-point/patch lineage drill-ins.
Use `inspector_target = usage` for graph/node/attempt pivots that keep the same object but focus the usage section.
Keep all message-step-line-range style anchors out of `inspector_target`.
Explicitly state that workspace-tab selection, panel docking, and per-project layout restore are shell-state concerns layered underneath canonical routing.
Treat commands like `cmd.panel.switch` as shell/view commands that can consume normalized routing context, not replace it.
Keep shell/workspace persistence in the shell/storage docs, not in the base route contract.
Allow the route model to name major destination surfaces/tabs/panels where operationally necessary.
This seam prevents the route model from swallowing the whole shell. The right question for routing is 'where should the user land,' not 'how should every panel be laid out when they get there.'
Keep `active_subview`, filters, compare targets, pinned selections, and similar fields in destination/view-state contracts.
Let routes optionally name a destination-local subview only when that is necessary for the task, but treat it as destination refinement, not base identity.
Reuse persisted project/surface state when the route does not specify a destination-local override.
The route model should be able to land a user in Source Control without becoming a full serialized `source_control.project_state`.
Publish a single superseding canonical payload block in Contracts_V0.md for scheduler/safe-point/remediation records and explicitly demote older variants
Add a canonical actor envelope shared by runtime records, provider-account snapshots, receipts, Usage pivots, and conversational actor telemetry
Normalize cross-surface receipt records so project_id, actor refs, created_at_utc, and usage_event_ref are required whenever a surface may pivot historically or across projects
Define usage_event_ref once as a locator-grade canonical reference and reuse it everywhere rather than inventing a new opaque ID family
Normalize Run Graph onto canonical cmd.runtime.* / cmd.orchestrator.open_in_* command bindings, add the missing action envelope, and add trust-state gating rules
Allow short-term concern rendering to piggyback on finding_refs[], but define a minimal non-remediation node_concerns[] projection next
Pre-attempt blocked episodes still need blocked_sequence handling without fabricating attempt_id
usage_event_ref should be a structured locator, not just a display string
The contract now has enough shape to define concrete route normalization for the most common user-facing flows.

cost usage -> Show in Usage: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=usage_event`, `object_id=<canonical usage event id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread-scoped, `inspector_target=usage`
cost usage -> Show in Ledger: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=usage_event`, `object_id=<id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread-scoped, `tab_id=ledger`

wizard resume: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=wizard`, `object_id=<wizard_id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread must be restored; serialized `resume_url` carries narrow step anchor detail
chat search hit: `target_kind=side_panel`, `project_id=<id>`, `thread_id=<id>`, `object_kind=message`, `object_id=<message_id>`

node detail pivot: `target_kind=page_tab`, `project_id=<id>`, `focused_run_id=<run_id>`, `object_kind=node`, `object_id=<node_id>`, `tab_id=node_graph`, `inspector_target=details|evidence|usage|history`
command discoverability does not weaken confirmation requirements
strong/hard_gate/non_reversible/compensating_action_only actions must still honor same gating and preview requirements via palette and shortcut surfaces
palette-friendly: open/focus tab, jump to run/seam/package/node/lane/concern/review/patch/recovery, open inspector, run search routes, low-risk view and filter commands
palette-allowed but guarded: recover/retry/approve/decline/replan/restore/cleanup with canonical runtime semantics and confirmation rules
palette-discouraged or hidden by default: broad destructive bulk mutations with ambiguous target sets
